title: Reading stems: keyword cues and eliminating distractors

kcs.statement: Qualifier phrases decide the answer: 'least operational overhead' points to a managed or serverless service, and 'most cost-effective' points to the cheapest option that still meets every stated requirement.

Distractors are usually real AWS services that do a different job or belong to a different category, so eliminating them first typically leaves two options to compare against the stem's exact requirement.
A multiple-response item states how many options to select (two or more out of five or more) and earns credit only when every option you choose is correct.

problem_ideas: A stem asks for a relational database with the least operational overhead; options are MySQL on EC2, RDS, DynamoDB and Redshift; eliminate two and pick one.
Underline the qualifier in five stems ('most cost-effective', 'highly available', 'least effort', 'without managing servers', 'global users') and name the service family each points to.
A 'Select TWO' question about increasing availability: choose the two correct options out of five and explain why the attractive third one is wrong.
Rewrite a distractor so that it would become the correct answer, showing which requirement it fails today.
A stem asks for the cheapest storage for data read once a year with 12-hour retrieval allowed; eliminate S3 Standard and EFS and justify the choice.
Spot the trap: the stem says 'without provisioning servers' and the options include EC2 Auto Scaling and Lambda.
Classify three wrong options in a missed question as 'wrong category', 'wrong job' or 'fails a qualifier'.
